correctness.rationale: The central moments are independently derived from exact horizontal sections and match the polynomial formulas in RESULT.md. For every a,b>0 and t>0, J'(t)=-t sum(c_k t^k)/A^5, and all seven c_k are strictly positive using 157/50<pi<22/7, proving global strict decrease. The normalized starting and limiting disk values and signed short/long expansions are exact and checked against independent slice integrals. The symbolic certificate verifies all coefficients; finite quadrature is supplemental.

evidence: The quermassintegral quotient is monotone for arbitrary parallel bodies but the covariance determinant involves non-quermass moments. The first-variation formula in Kipp 2023 does not determine the sign after t>0.

The square and regular-polygon results establish strict decrease only for equal-side regular polygons. An unequal rectangle is affinely a square, but its Euclidean disk-rounding pulls back to anisotropic ellipse-rounding; neither previous statement covers this.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Non-square all-radius strictness is not a substitution into the square/cube result. The proof supplies a new positive bivariate polynomial derivative certificate, and the near-zero universal curvature is supported independently.

evidence: For a centrally symmetric rectangle, the invariant is M_x M_y/A^4, not its polar moment alone. Richter–Saorín Gómez treat S(K_t)^2/A(K_t) and mixed-volume quotients (arXiv:2003.14182, Sections 3 and 5). Kipp’s first-order criterion at an isotropic point is a derivative at t=0 (arXiv:2303.18033, Section 1).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Equivalent formulations include normalized squared inertia-axis product, covariance determinant and fourth power of the planar isotropic constant. None of the read statements gives the all-radius derivative sign for unequal rectangles. Square rounding by a disk is already a regular-polygon special case but does not imply unequal aspect ratios via affine maps because the disk then becomes an ellipse.

originality.rationale: The new all-radius, all-aspect-ratio rectangular covariance determinant law is not implied by the checked isoperimetric-quermassintegral theory, first-order isotropic perturbation results, cubical local-rounding theorem, or regular-polygon parallel-body profile. The square subcase and moment ingredients are acknowledged rather than claimed new. Exact older inertia profiles or unindexed monotonicity statements remain residual risks.
residual_risks: Searches and inspected primary texts cannot rule out an unindexed mechanical-inertia monotonicity calculation or a generalized invariant-ordering result under different terminology.
A separately established regular-polygon parallel-body profile includes the square subcase; the new mathematical content is its extension to all unequal rectangles.
Material for the engineering corner-rounding page is limited to accessible webpage text; it does not resolve historical coverage by all engineering handbooks.

value.rationale: The result provides a complete strict ordering for the full two-parameter family of positive rectangles, including unbounded aspect ratios and all rounding radii, under a natural affine invariant. It identifies a universal short-radius curvature under area-normalized distance and sharp disk-endpoint approach. It is not just a square specialization or a single tabulated moment; no all-convex-body statement or external importance is asserted.
